channel.description: Recent content in Microsoft Security Blog on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes a human-operated campaign that uses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support, obtain remote access, and deploy a Node.js-based implant. The post also explains how attackers use legitimate tools for lateral movement and how Microsoft Defender can help detect and disrupt the activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Hunting MacSync Stealer infrastructure through behavioral pivots
item.description:
Microsoft describes how it tracked MacSync Stealer infrastructure despite rapid domain rotation by using stable behavioral pivots. The investigation identified more than 30 related domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
Microsoft describes a macOS ClickFix campaign that changed from openly delivering infostealer lures to placing them behind a browser-fingerprinting gate. The shift reduces visibility of the malicious infrastructure but also creates new detection opportunities for defenders.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Microsoft reports that Q2 2026 saw continued declines in several phishing techniques after disruption of the Tycoon2FA platform. Attackers shifted toward Teams-based social engineering and more automated, multi-stage attack chains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: 5 insights from Frost & Sullivan’s 2025 Frost Radar™ for Cloud Security Posture Management
item.description:
Microsoft summarizes five takeaways from Frost & Sullivan’s 2025 Frost Radar for Cloud Security Posture Management, highlighting a shift from point-in-time compliance to continuous risk management. The post frames CSPM as evolving toward broader, ongoing cloud security oversight.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
item.description:
The post explains MCP tool poisoning as an attack that can turn trusted AI agents into a control plane for data loss. It describes how attackers manipulate tool descriptions to induce unauthorized actions, and outlines detection, containment, and prevention approaches.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: One intrusion, two cyberattackers: Uncovering parallel threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft describes a ransomware case where two threat actors operated in parallel during the same intrusion, using overlapping tactics and evasion methods. The report emphasizes that isolated telemetry can miss complex attacks when activity from multiple actors is blended together.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering
item.description:
Threat actors are using AI-related brands and public interest in AI as social engineering lures. Microsoft says attackers are both operationalizing AI to speed up attacks and exploiting AI hype to make scams more convincing.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
